ordered_diagnoses: Hepatic vein thrombosis due to membranous obstruction

s1.syndrome_frame: subacute febrile illness with back pain and multiple organ involvement
salient_findings: fever and back pain lasting 3 weeks
key_facts: 76-year-old Japanese man
presented with fever and back pain
endoscopic treatment for common bile duct stones 3 weeks prior
medical history of diabetes mellitus and hypertension
taking cilnidipine and metformin hydrochloride
smoking 20 cigarettes per day for 47 years
consuming 70g of ethanol daily
elevated CRP (22.1 mg/dL) and WBC (11,910/μL)
low platelet count (10.3 × 104/μL)
elevated ALP (275 U/L) and low albumin (1.7 g/dL)
abnormal liver imaging with two hypodense lesions in the right liver lobe
multiple cavitated nodules in lungs on CT and MRI
thrombosis of hepatic vein on CT and MRI
low-density area of left-sided iliopsoas muscle swelling on CT and MRI
enlarged high-signal areas in L4/5 intervertebral disc on MRI
gram-negative bacilli on Gram staining
positive cultures (blood, urine, and abscess fluid) for identified organism

shortlist.label: Klebsiella pneumoniae liver abscess
shortlist.why_kept: elevated CRP, WBC, and abnormal liver imaging with hypodense lesions, along with gram-negative bacilli on Gram staining and positive cultures

shortlist.why_kept: thrombosis of hepatic vein on CT and MRI, which could be related to the patient's condition

shortlist.label: Infective Endocarditis

shortlist.label: Pott's Disease
shortlist.why_kept: back pain and abnormal imaging findings, including low-density area of left-sided iliopsoas muscle swelling and enlarged high-signal areas in L4/5 intervertebral disc

raw.rationale: The patient has elevated CRP and WBC, low platelet count, and abnormal liver imaging with two hypodense lesions in the right liver lobe, which are consistent with a liver abscess. The presence of gram-negative bacilli on Gram staining and positive cultures for the identified organism also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Hepatic vein thrombosis due to membranous obstruction
rejected.why: While the patient has thrombosis of the hepatic vein, the presence of a liver abscess and positive cultures suggest an infectious cause rather than a membranous obstruction.

rejected.label: Infective Endocarditis
rejected.why: There is no heart murmur, Osler's nodes, or Janeway lesions present, which are common findings in infective endocarditis.

rejected.label: Pott's Disease
rejected.why: The patient has no muscle weakness or sensory impairments, and the Straight Leg Raise test is negative, which makes Pott's disease less likely.

rejected.label: Nocardiosis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results do not specifically suggest Nocardiosis, and the presence of gram-negative bacilli on Gram staining is more consistent with a Klebsiella pneumoniae infection.

gold: Pyogenic liver abscess caused by Klebsiella oxytoca with metastatic complications (septic pulmonary embolism, right hepatic vein thrombosis, spondylodiscitis, and retroperitoneal abscess)
